title.zh: 卷十 補列傳第二 高祖十一王
title.en: Volume 10 Biographies 2: Eleven Princes of Shenwu
title.raw: 卷十 補列傳第二 高祖十一王 Volume 10 Biographies 2: Eleven Princes of Shenwu

sentences.zh: 高祖十一王

translations.literal: The Eleven Princes of Gaozu
translations.idiomatic: The Eleven Princes of Shenwu

sentences.zh: 永安簡平王浚 平陽靖翼王淹 彭城景思王浟 上党剛肅王渙 襄城景王淯 任城王湝 高陽康穆王湜 博陵文簡王濟 華山王凝 馮翊王潤 漢陽敬懷王洽

translations.literal: Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You; Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu; Prince of Rencheng Hui; Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Prince of Huashan Ning; Prince of Fengyi Run; Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianping of Yong'an (Jun); Prince Jingyi of Pingyang (Yan); Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng (You); Prince Gangsu of Shangdang (Huan); Prince Jing of Xiangcheng (Yu); Prince of Rencheng (Hui); Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang (Shi); Prince Wenjian of Boling (Ji); Prince of Huashan (Ning); Prince of Fengyi (Run); Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang (Qia)

sentences.zh: 神武皇帝十五男：武明婁皇后生文襄皇帝、文宣皇帝、孝昭皇帝、襄城景王淯、武成皇帝、博陵文簡王濟，王氏生永安簡平王浚，穆氏生平陽靖翼王淹，大尒朱氏生彭城景思王浟、華山王凝，韓氏生上党剛肅王渙，小尒朱氏生任城王湝，游氏生高陽康穆王湜，鄭氏生馮翊王潤，馮氏生漢陽敬懷王洽。

translations.literal: The Shenwu Emperor had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Emperor Wenxiang, Emperor Wenxuan, Emperor Xiaozhao, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Emperor Wucheng, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Hui; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, the Shenwu Emperor, had fifteen sons: Empress Wuming née Lou bore Gao Cheng, Gao Yang, Gao Yan, Prince Jing of Xiangcheng Yu, Gao Zhan, and Prince Wenjian of Boling Ji; Lady Wang bore Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince Jingyi of Pingyang Yan; the Grand Lady Erzhu bore Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You and Prince of Huashan Ning; Lady Han bore Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan; the Lesser Lady Erzhu bore Prince of Rencheng Hui; Lady You bore Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang Shi; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Fengyi Run; Lady Feng bore Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang Qia.

sentences.zh: 永安簡平王浚，字定樂，神武第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jianping of Yong'an, Jun, style name Dingle, was the third son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianping of Yong'an (Jun), whose style name was Dingle, was the third son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 初，神武納浚母，當月而有孕，及產浚，疑非己類，不甚愛之。

translations.literal: At first, when Shenwu took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born, he suspected the child was not of his kind and did not love him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan first took Jun's mother into his household, she conceived that same month; when Jun was born he doubted the child was truly his and showed little affection.

sentences.zh: 而浚早慧，後更被寵。

translations.literal: Yet Jun was precocious, and afterward came to be favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jun was precocious, and in time he came to be favored.

sentences.zh: 年八歲時，問于博士盧景裕曰：「『祭神如神在。

translations.literal: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.'
translations.idiomatic: At eight years of age he asked the Erudite Lu Jingyu, saying, " 'One sacrifices to the spirits as though the spirits were present.'

sentences.zh: 』為有神邪，無神邪？

translations.literal: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"
translations.idiomatic: Is there a spirit, or is there not?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰；

translations.literal: He replied:
translations.idiomatic: He replied:

translations.literal: "There is."
translations.idiomatic: "There is."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「有神當雲祭神神在，何煩『如』字？

translations.literal: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "If there is a spirit, one ought simply to say 'One sacrifices to the spirits; the spirits are present' — why bother with the word 'as though'?"

sentences.zh: 」景裕不能答。

translations.literal: Jingyu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu could not answer.

sentences.zh: 及長，嬉戲不節，曾以屬請受納，大見杖罰，拘禁府獄，旣而見原。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was heavily beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he played without restraint; once he used his influence to solicit bribes and was severely beaten and cane-punished, confined in the princely prison, and afterward pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後稍折節，頗以讀書為務。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat reformed his ways and took reading as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he somewhat reformed his conduct and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 元象中，封永安郡公。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 豪爽有氣力，善騎射，為文襄所愛。

translations.literal: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and open, possessed of strength, skilled at riding and archery — he was loved by Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 文宣性雌懦，每參文襄，有時涕出。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's nature was timid and weak; whenever he attended upon Wenxiang, tears sometimes fell.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang was by nature timid and effeminate; whenever he attended upon Gao Cheng, tears would sometimes fall.

sentences.zh: 浚常責帝左右，何因不為二兄拭鼻，由是見銜。

translations.literal: Jun often rebuked those at the Emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe the elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.
translations.idiomatic: Jun often rebuked those at the emperor's side, asking why they did not wipe his elder brothers' noses for them — on this account he came to be resented.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書監、兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為青州刺史，頗好畋獵，聰明矜恕，上下畏悅之。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting; intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Qing Province; he was rather fond of hunting, yet intelligent, stern yet forgiving — high and low both feared and delighted in him.

sentences.zh: 天保初，進爵為王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was advanced to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年多酒，浚謂親近曰：「二兄舊來不甚了了，自登祚已後，識解頓進。

translations.literal: In the last years of Wenxuan's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Gao Yang's reign he drank heavily; Jun said to those close to him, "My two elder brothers were never very clear-minded before; since ascending the throne their understanding has suddenly advanced.

sentences.zh: 今因酒敗德，朝臣無敢諫者，大敵未滅，吾甚以為憂，欲乘驛至鄴面諫，不知用吾不。

translations.literal: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will use me."
translations.idiomatic: Now through wine he ruins his virtue, yet none of the court ministers dare remonstrate. The great enemy is not yet destroyed — I am deeply troubled; I wish to take post-horses to Ye and remonstrate face to face — I do not know whether they will heed me."

sentences.zh: 」人有知，密以白帝，又見銜。

translations.literal: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the Emperor, and again he came to be resented.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who knew of it secretly reported to the emperor, and again he came to be resented.

sentences.zh: 八年來朝，從幸東山。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the Emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court and accompanied the emperor on an excursion to Eastern Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝裸裎為樂，雜以婦女，又作狐掉尾戲。

translations.literal: The Emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped naked for amusement, mingling with women, and also performed the fox-tail dance.

sentences.zh: 浚進言此非人主所宜。

translations.literal: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Jun remonstrated that this was not fitting for a ruler.

sentences.zh: 帝甚不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 浚又于屏處召楊遵彥，譏其不諫。

translations.literal: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also summoned Yang Zunyan in a secluded place and mocked him for not remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 帝時不欲大臣與諸王交通，遵彥懼以奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at that time did not wish great ministers to have dealings with the princes; Zunyan, in fear, reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「小人由來難忍！

translations.literal: The Emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "Such petty men have always been intolerable!"

sentences.zh: 」遂罷酒還宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ended the feast and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 浚尋還州，又上書切諫。

translations.literal: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun soon returned to his province and again submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 詔令徵浚，浚懼禍，謝疾不至。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Jun; Jun, fearing disaster, pleaded illness and did not come.

sentences.zh: 上怒，馳驛收浚，老幼泣送者數千人。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent post-horses to seize Jun; old and young wept as they saw him off — several thousand in number.

sentences.zh: 至，盛以鐵籠，與上黨王渙俱置北城地牢下，飲食溲穢共在一所。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Gangsu of Shangdang Huan, was put in an underground dungeon beneath the northern city wall; food, drink, urine, and filth were all in one place.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝親將左右臨穴歌謳，令浚和之。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor personally led his attendants to the pit to sing and chant, ordering Jun to harmonize with him.

sentences.zh: 浚等惶怖且悲，不覺聲戰。

translations.literal: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and the others were terrified and grief-stricken; without knowing it their voices trembled.

sentences.zh: 帝為愴然，因泣，將赦之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to sorrow and wept, intending to pardon them.

sentences.zh: 長廣王湛先與浚不睦，進曰：「猛獸安可出穴。

translations.literal: Prince Changguang Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "Can a fierce beast safely be let out of its den?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changguang Gao Zhan, who had long been on bad terms with Jun, stepped forward and said, "Can a fierce beast safely be let out of its den?"

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 浚等聞之，呼長廣小字曰：「步落稽，皇天見汝！

translations.literal: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jun and the others heard it, they cried out Changguang's childhood name: "Buluoji — Heaven sees you!"

sentences.zh: 」左右聞者，莫不悲傷。

translations.literal: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Those among the attendants who heard it — none was not grief-stricken.

sentences.zh: 浚與渙皆有雄略，為諸王所傾服，帝恐為害，乃自刺渙，又使壯土劉桃枝就籠亂刺。

translations.literal: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the Emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Huan both possessed bold strategy and were admired and submitted to by the princes; the emperor feared they would do harm and therefore personally stabbed Huan, then had the strong man Liu Taozhi enter the cage and stab wildly.

sentences.zh: 槊每下，浚、渙輒以手拉折之，號哭呼天。

translations.literal: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the spear descended, Jun and Huan would grasp it and break it off with their hands, crying out and calling to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 於是薪火亂投，燒殺之，填以石土。

translations.literal: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon firewood was thrown in confusion and they were burned to death, then covered with stone and earth.

sentences.zh: 後出，皮髮皆盡，屍色如炭，天下為之痛心。

translations.literal: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.
translations.idiomatic: When they were later dug out, skin and hair were entirely gone and the corpses were black as charcoal; the realm was heart-stricken on their account.

sentences.zh: 後帝以其妃陸氏配儀同劉郁捷，舊帝蒼頭也，以軍功見用，時令郁捷害浚，故以配焉。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor gave Jun's consort Lady Lu in marriage to Palace Attendant Equal to the Third Rank Liu Yujie — a former personal attendant of the Emperor who had been employed for military merit; at the time he had ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and therefore she was given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor gave Jun's consort Lady Lu in marriage to Palace Attendant Equal to the Third Rank Liu Yujie — a former personal attendant of the emperor who had been employed for military merit; at the time he had ordered Yujie to kill Jun, and therefore she was given to him.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝以陸氏先無寵於浚，勑與離絕。

translations.literal: Several days later the Emperor, because Lady Lu had never been favored by Jun, ordered that the marriage be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the emperor, because Lady Lu had never been favored by Jun, ordered that the marriage be severed.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianming he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔以彭城王浟第二子準嗣。

translations.literal: Having no sons, an edict appointed Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You's second son Zhun as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no sons, an edict appointed Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng You's second son Zhun as heir.

sentences.zh: 彭城景思王浟，字子深，神武第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng, You, style name Zishen, was the fifth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingsi of Pengcheng (You), whose style name was Zishen, was the fifth son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 元象二年，拜通直散騎常侍，封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxiang he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yuanxiang era he was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Duke of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 博士韓毅教浟書，見浟筆跡未工，戲浟曰：「五郎書畫如此，忽為常侍開國，今日後宜更用心。

translations.literal: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."
translations.idiomatic: The Erudite Han Yi taught You to write; seeing that You's handwriting was not yet skilled, he joked with You, saying, "Fifth Lord's writing and drawing are like this — suddenly to become Regular Attendant and establish a state, from today onward you ought to apply yourself more diligently."

sentences.zh: 」浟正色答曰：「昔甘羅幼為秦相，未聞能書。

translations.literal: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.
translations.idiomatic: You replied with a stern countenance, "In former times Gan Luo in youth became Chancellor of Qin — one never heard that he could write.

sentences.zh: 凡人唯論才具何如，豈必動誇筆跡。

translations.literal: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like — why must one always boast of one's handwriting?
translations.idiomatic: For a man one considers only what his talents and capacity are like — why must one always boast of one's handwriting?

sentences.zh: 博士當今能者，何為不作三公？

translations.literal: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Erudite is so capable today, why does he not become one of the Three Excellencies?"

sentences.zh: 」時年蓋八歲矣。

translations.literal: He was then about eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was then about eight years old.

sentences.zh: 毅甚慚。

translations.literal: Yi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 武定六年，出為滄州刺史，為政嚴察，部內肅然。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Wuding era he went out as Governor of Cang Prefecture; his governance was strict and searching, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.

sentences.zh: 守令參佐，下及胥吏，行遊往來，皆自賚糧食。

translations.literal: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects, magistrates, aides, and subordinates, down to clerks and petty officials — all who traveled on business brought their own provisions.

sentences.zh: 浟纖介知人間事。

translations.literal: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.
translations.idiomatic: You knew of the smallest matters among the people.

sentences.zh: 有濕沃縣主簿張達嘗詣州，夜投人舍，食雞羹，浟察知之。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk of Shiwo County, Zhang Da, once came to the province; at night he lodged in a private house and ate chicken broth — You detected it.

sentences.zh: 守令畢集，浟對衆曰：「食雞羹何不還價直也？

translations.literal: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"
translations.idiomatic: When the prefects and magistrates had all assembled, You said before the crowd, "You ate chicken broth — why did you not pay the price?"

sentences.zh: 」達卽伏罪。

translations.literal: Da immediately confessed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Da immediately confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 合境號為神明。

translations.literal: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The entire jurisdiction called him divine in judgment.

sentences.zh: 又有一人從幽州來，驢馱鹿脯。

translations.literal: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man who came from You Province, his donkey laden with dried venison.

sentences.zh: 至滄州界，腳痛行遲，偶會一人為伴，遂盜驢及脯去。

translations.literal: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border of Cang Prefecture his foot ached and he walked slowly; by chance he met a man who became his traveling companion, and that man stole the donkey and the venison and fled.

sentences.zh: 明旦，告州。

translations.literal: The next morning he reported it to the province.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he reported it to the province.

sentences.zh: 浟乃令左右及府僚吏分市鹿脯，不限其價。

translations.literal: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.
translations.idiomatic: You then ordered his attendants and provincial staff to buy dried venison in the markets, without limiting the price.

sentences.zh: 其主見脯識之，推獲盜者。

translations.literal: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.
translations.idiomatic: The owner saw the venison and recognized it; pursuing it, he captured the thief.

sentences.zh: 轉都督、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be Area Commander and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 時有人被盜黑牛，背上有白毛。

translations.literal: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man had a black ox stolen; on its back there was white hair.

sentences.zh: 長史韋道建謂中從事魏道勝曰：「使君在滄州日，擒姦如神，若捉得此賊，定神矣。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei Daojian said to Senior Clerk Wei Daosheng, "When the lord was in Cang Prefecture he captured wrongdoers like a spirit; if he catches this thief, he will surely be divine."

sentences.zh: 」浟乃詐為上府市牛皮，倍酬價直，使牛主認之，因獲其盜。

translations.literal: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.
translations.idiomatic: You then falsely announced that the superior office was buying ox hides in the market, paying double the price, and had the ox's owner identify them — thereby capturing the thief.

sentences.zh: 建等歎服。

translations.literal: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Daojian and the others sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 又有老母姓王，孤獨，種菜三畝，數被偷。

translations.literal: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: There was also an old woman surnamed Wang, alone and without support, who planted vegetables on three mu; they were stolen repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 浟乃令人密往書菜葉為字，明日市中看菜葉有字，獲賊。

translations.literal: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.
translations.idiomatic: You then had men secretly go and write characters on the vegetable leaves; the next day, seeing characters on the leaves in the market, they captured the thief.

sentences.zh: 爾後境內無盜，政化為當時第一。

translations.literal: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.
translations.idiomatic: After that there were no thieves within the borders, and his governance and transformation ranked first in the age.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封彭城王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，徵為侍中，人吏送別悲號。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant; officials and commoners saw him off with wailing lament.

sentences.zh: 有老公數百人相率具饌曰：「自殿下至來五載，人不識吏，吏不欺人，百姓有識已來，始逢今化。

translations.literal: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred old men together prepared provisions and said, "From the time Your Highness arrived until now, five years — the people do not know officials, and officials do not deceive the people; from the time the common people have had understanding until now, they have only now encountered such transformation.

sentences.zh: 殿下唯飲此鄉水，未食此鄉食，聊獻疏薄。

translations.literal: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has only drunk this district's water and has not yet eaten this district's food — we humbly offer this poor fare."

sentences.zh: 」浟重其意，為食一口。

translations.literal: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.
translations.idiomatic: You, honoring their intent, ate one mouthful.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉司州牧，選從事皆取文才士明剖斷者，當時稱為美選。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Governor of Si Province; in selecting aides he took only men of literary talent skilled in clear judgment — at the time this was called a fine selection.

sentences.zh: 州舊案五百餘，浟未期悉斷盡。

translations.literal: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.
translations.idiomatic: The province had more than five hundred old cases; before the term was out You had judged them all.

sentences.zh: 別駕羊脩等恐犯權戚，乃詣閤諮陳。

translations.literal: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Prefect Yang Xiu and others, fearing they might offend powerful kin, therefore came to the gate to consult and report.

sentences.zh: 浟使告曰：「吾直道而行，何憚權戚，卿等當成人之美，反以權戚為言。

translations.literal: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."
translations.idiomatic: You sent word saying, "I walk the straight path — why should I fear powerful kin? You ought to help others achieve excellence; instead you speak of powerful kin."

sentences.zh: 」脩等慚悚而退。

translations.literal: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu and the others withdrew in shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 後加特進，兼司空、太尉，州牧如故。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was additionally appointed Special Advancement, Concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Commandant, his governorship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太妃薨，解任，尋詔復本官。

translations.literal: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Princess Consort died he was relieved of office; soon an edict restored him to his original post.

sentences.zh: 俄拜司空，兼尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 濟南嗣位，除開府儀同三司、尚書令、領大宗正卿。

translations.literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, he was removed to Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，拜大司馬，兼尚書令，轉太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was appointed Grand Marshal and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 武成入承大業，遷太師、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Wucheng succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhan succeeded to the great enterprise, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 浟明練世務，果於斷決，事無大小，咸悉以情。

translations.literal: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.
translations.idiomatic: You was clear and practiced in affairs of the age, decisive in judgment; matters great and small he handled entirely according to the merits of each case.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李公統預高歸彥之逆，其母崔氏卽御史中丞崔昂從父子，兼右僕射魏收之內妹也。

translations.literal: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongtong of Zhao Commandery took part in Gao Guiyan's rebellion; his mother Lady Cui was the daughter of a younger cousin of Censor-in-Chief Cui Ang, and also the younger sister by marriage of Right Vice Director Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 依令，年出六十，例免入官。

translations.literal: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.
translations.idiomatic: According to the statute, those over sixty years of age were by rule exempt from being taken into official service.

sentences.zh: 崔增年陳訴，所司以昂、收故，崔遂獲免。

translations.literal: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Cui added years to her age and submitted a petition; the responsible office, because of Ang and Shou, therefore exempted Cui.

sentences.zh: 浟摘發其事，昂等以罪除名。

translations.literal: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: You exposed the matter; Ang and the others were stripped of their names and offices on account of the crime.

sentences.zh: 自車駕巡幸，浟常留鄴。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, You often remained at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, You often remained at Ye.

sentences.zh: 河清三年三月，群盜田子禮等數十人謀劫浟為主，詐稱使者，徑向浟第，至內室，稱勑牽浟上馬，臨以白刃，欲引向南殿。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Heqing, several dozen bandits including Tian Zili plotted to seize You as their leader; falsely claiming to be envoys, they went straight to You's residence, entered the inner chamber, declared an edict, dragged You onto a horse, threatened him with naked blades, and wished to lead him to the Southern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of the Heqing era, several dozen bandits led by Tian Zili plotted to make You their figurehead; posing as imperial envoys, they went straight to his residence, entered the inner chamber, declared an edict, dragged him onto a horse, held blades to his throat, and tried to march him toward the Southern Hall.

sentences.zh: 浟大呼不從，遂遇害，時年三十二，朝野痛惜焉。

translations.literal: You cried out in refusal and would not submit; he was thereupon murdered. He was thirty-two years of age; court and realm alike mourned him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: You shouted his refusal and would not submit; he was murdered on the spot. He was thirty-two. Court and realm mourned.

sentences.zh: 初浟未被劫前，其妃鄭氏夢人斬浟頭持去，惡之，數日而浟見殺。

translations.literal: Before You was seized, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed that a man cut off You's head and carried it away; she found it ominous, and within several days You was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the attack, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed of a man severing You's head and carrying it away; she took it as an ill omen, and within days You was dead.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉、錄尚書事，給轀輬車。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and given an imperial mourning carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, grand commandant, and recorder of the Masters of Writing, with an imperial mourning carriage.

sentences.zh: 子寶德嗣，位開府，兼尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His son Baode succeeded him, holding the rank of Opener of the Way and Concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baode succeeded, serving as opener of the way and concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 上黨剛肅王渙，字敬壽，神武第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, style name Jingshou, was the seventh son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang (Huan), whose style name was Jingshou, was the seventh son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 天姿雄傑，俶儻不群，雖在童幼，恒以將略自許。

translations.literal: By nature he was heroic and outstanding, daring and unlike others; even in childhood he always reckoned himself destined for generalship.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally heroic and bold, unmatched even in boyhood, he always counted himself born for command.

sentences.zh: 神武壯而愛之，曰：「此兒似我。

translations.literal: Shenwu, impressed, loved him and said, "This boy is like me."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan admired him and said, "This boy is my image."

sentences.zh: 」及長，力能扛鼎，材武絕倫。

translations.literal: When he grew up he could lift a tripod; in talent and martial prowess he was without peer.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he could lift a bronze tripod; in arms and valor none could match him.

sentences.zh: 每謂左右曰：「人不可無學，但要不為博士耳。

translations.literal: He often told those at his side, "A man must not be without learning — only he need not become an Erudite."
translations.idiomatic: He often told his attendants, "A man must have learning — he need only avoid becoming a pedant."

sentences.zh: 」故讀書頗知梗概，而不甚耽習。

translations.literal: Therefore he read books and knew the outlines of things, but was not deeply devoted to study.
translations.idiomatic: He read enough to grasp the main points, but never lost himself in books.

sentences.zh: 元象中，封平原郡公。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文襄之遇賊，渙年尚幼，在西學，聞宮中嘩，驚曰：「大兄必遭難矣！

translations.literal: When Wenxiang met with assassins, Huan was still young and at the Western Academy; hearing an uproar in the palace, he started and said, "Eldest brother must have met disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng fell to assassins, Huan was still a boy at the Western Academy; hearing uproar in the palace, he cried, "Eldest brother has met disaster!"

sentences.zh: 」彎弓而出。

translations.literal: He strung his bow and rushed out.
translations.idiomatic: He strung his bow and ran out.

sentences.zh: 武定末，除冀州刺史，在州有美政。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed Governor of Ji Province and governed the province with distinction.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed governor of Ji Province and governed with distinction.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封上党王，歷中書令、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and served successively as Director of the Secretariat and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and rose through director of the Secretariat and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 與常山王演等築伐惡諸城。

translations.literal: Together with Prince of Changshan Yan and others he built fortified camps to attack the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Changshan Gao Yan and others he built fortified camps for punitive raids.

sentences.zh: 遂聚鄴下輕薄，淩犯郡縣，為法司所糾。

translations.literal: He then gathered rowdies beneath Ye, who harassed the commanderies and counties and were reported by the judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered ruffians from Ye who harassed the counties and were denounced by the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 文宣戮其左右數人，渙亦被譴。

translations.literal: Wenxuan executed several of his attendants and reprimanded Huan as well.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang executed several of his attendants and rebuked Huan himself.

sentences.zh: 六年，率衆送梁王蕭明還江南，仍破東關，斬梁特進裴之橫等，威名甚盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led troops escorting Liang's Prince Xiao Ming back to Jiangnan, and also broke through Dong Pass, slaying Liang's Special Advance Pei Zhiheng and others; his fame was at its height.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he escorted Liang's Prince Xiao Ming south to Jiangnan, broke Dong Pass, and slew Liang's special advance Pei Zhiheng and others — his fame standing at its height.

sentences.zh: 八年，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，術士言亡高者黑衣，由是自神武后，每出行，不欲見沙門，為黑衣故也。

translations.literal: At first diviners had said that the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; hence after Shenwu, whenever they went abroad they did not wish to meet Buddhist monks, because monks wore black.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners had once said the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; after Gao Huan's death the court on its travels avoided Buddhist monks for that reason.

sentences.zh: 是時文宣幸晉陽，以所忌問左右曰：「何物最黑？

translations.literal: At that time Wenxuan was at Jinyang; following his superstition he asked those at his side, "What thing is blackest?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang was then at Jinyang; acting on this fear he asked his attendants, "What is blackest of all?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「莫過漆。

translations.literal: They answered, "Nothing blacker than lacquer."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Nothing surpasses lacquer."

sentences.zh: 」帝以渙第七子為當之，乃使庫真都督破六韓伯昇之鄴徵渙。

translations.literal: The Emperor decided that Huan as the seventh son must be the omen, and sent Storehouse Commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decided Huan, as the seventh son, must be the omen, and sent storehouse commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon him.

sentences.zh: 渙至紫陌橋，殺伯昇以逃，憑河而度，土人執以送帝。

translations.literal: When Huan reached Zimo Bridge he killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At Zimo Bridge Huan killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 鐵籠盛之，與永安王浚同置地牢下。

translations.literal: He was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun, was put in an underground dungeon.
translations.idiomatic: He was caged in iron and shut in the underground dungeon with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，與浚同見殺，時年二十六。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 以其妃李氏配馮文洛，是帝家舊奴，積勞位至刺史，帝令文洛等殺渙，故以其妻妻焉。

translations.literal: His consort Lady Li was given in marriage to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to governor; the Emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and therefore gave him Huan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Li was given to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to provincial governor; the emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and so gave him Huan's wife.

sentences.zh: 至乾明元年，收二王餘骨葬之，贈司空，諡曰剛肅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianming the scattered bones of the two princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous name Gangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era the scattered bones of both princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously made minister of works with the posthumous name Gangsu.

sentences.zh: 有勑李氏還第。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lady Li to return to her residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lady Li back to her own residence.

sentences.zh: 而文洛尚以故意，修飾詣李，李盛列左右，引文洛立於階下，數之曰：「遭難流離，以至大辱，志操寡薄，不能自盡，幸蒙恩詔，得反藩闈。

translations.literal: Wenluo, still bearing his old grudge, dressed himself finely and came calling on Lady Li; she arrayed attendants on either side, summoned Wenluo to stand below the steps, and reproached him, saying, "Through calamity and exile I suffered the deepest shame; my resolve was too weak and I could not end my own life — by the grace of an edict I was allowed to return to my household.
translations.idiomatic: Wenluo, still nursing his old grievance, dressed finely and came to call; Lady Li arrayed her attendants, had Wenluo stand below the steps, and upbraided him: "Cast into calamity and exile, I suffered unspeakable shame; my spirit was too weak to die, and only by grace of an edict could I return home.

sentences.zh: 汝是誰家孰奴，猶欲見侮！

translations.literal: What sort of household slave are you, that you still dare show yourself to insult me!"
translations.idiomatic: What household wretch are you, to dare present yourself and insult me again!"

sentences.zh: 」於是杖之一百，流血灑地。

translations.literal: She then had him beaten a hundred strokes until blood pooled on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: She had him beaten a hundred strokes until blood spread across the floor.

sentences.zh: 渙無嫡子，庶長子寶嚴以河清二年襲爵，位金紫光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Huan had no son by his principal wife; his eldest son by a concubine, Baoyan, inherited the title in the second year of Heqing, holding the ranks of Golden Chalice Grand Master of Splendor and Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had no son by his principal wife; Baoyan, eldest son by a concubine, inherited in the second year of the Heqing era as golden-chalice grand master of splendor and opener of the way equal in honor to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 亮字彥道，性恭孝，美風儀，好文學。

translations.literal: Liang, style name Yandao, was by nature respectful and filial, handsome in bearing, and fond of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, styled Yandao, was respectful and filial by nature, graceful in bearing, and devoted to letters.

sentences.zh: 為徐州刺史，坐奪商人財物免官。

translations.literal: As Governor of Xu Province he was dismissed for seizing merchants' goods.
translations.idiomatic: Made governor of Xu Province, he was dismissed for seizing merchants' property.

sentences.zh: 後主敗奔鄴，亮從焉，遷兼太尉、太傅。

translations.literal: When Houzhu was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang followed him and was promoted to Concurrent Grand Commandant and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang went with him and was made concurrent grand commandant and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 周師入鄴，亮於啟夏門拒守。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang held Qixia Gate in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang held Qixia Gate.

sentences.zh: 諸軍皆不戰而敗，周軍於諸城門皆入，亮軍方退走。

translations.literal: Every other army fled without fighting; Zhou soldiers entered through every gate, and only then did Liang's force withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The other armies broke without a fight; Zhou soldiers entered every gate before Liang's troops finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亮入太廟行馬內，慟哭拜辭，然後為周軍所執。

translations.literal: Liang entered the horse-course enclosure within the imperial temple, wept in lament and bowed his farewell, and was then seized by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liang entered the horse-course within the imperial temple, wept his farewell, and was then taken by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 入關，依例授儀同，分配遠邊，卒於龍州。

translations.literal: Taken west into Guan, he was granted the rank of Yitong by regulation, assigned to a distant frontier, and died at Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: Taken into Guan he received the rank of yitong by regulation, was posted to a distant frontier, and died at Long Province.

sentences.zh: 及安德王稱尊號於晉陽，使劉子昂修啟於湝：「至尊出奔，宗廟旣重，群公勸迫，權主號令，事甯終歸叔父。

translations.literal: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself emperor at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Hui, saying, "The sovereign has fled; the ancestral temple weighs heavily on us; the lords press us to act — we temporarily hold command, but in the end power must return to our uncle."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Hui: "The sovereign has fled, the ancestral temple hangs in the balance, the lords press us to act; we hold command only for the moment — in the end it must return to Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」湝曰：「我人臣，何容受此啟。

translations.literal: Hui said, "I am the emperor's subject — how could I accept such a memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I am the emperor's subject — how could I accept this?"

sentences.zh: 」執子昂送鄴。

translations.literal: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 帝至濟州，禪位於湝，啟竟不達。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Hui's favor, the memorial never reached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Hui's favor, the memorial never reached him.

sentences.zh: 湝與廣甯王孝珩于冀州召募得四萬餘人，拒周軍。

translations.literal: Hui and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning raised more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning mustered more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲來伐，先遣送書並赦詔，湝並沉諸井。

translations.literal: Zhou's Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, came to attack and first sent letters and an amnesty edict; Hui sank them all in a well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian marched against them, first sending letters and an amnesty edict; Hui drowned them all in a well.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，湝、孝珩俱被擒。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, Hui and Xiaogong were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Hui and Xiaogong were both taken.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「任城王何苦至此？

translations.literal: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it end like this?"

sentences.zh: 」湝曰：「下官神武帝子，兄弟十五人，幸而獨存，逢宗社顛覆，今日得死，無愧墳陵。

translations.literal: Hui said, "I am a subject-son of the Shenwu Emperor; of fifteen brothers I alone survived. To meet the dynasty's fall and die today — I need not blush before our tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I am a son of Gao Huan; of fifteen brothers I alone survive. To see the altars overturned and die today — I need feel no shame before our tombs."

sentences.zh: 」憲壯之，歸其妻子。

translations.literal: Xian admired his spirit and returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Xian admired his spirit and restored his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 將至鄴城，湝馬上大哭，自投於地，流血滿面。

translations.literal: As they neared Ye city, Hui wept aloud on horseback and threw himself to the ground, blood streaming down his face.
translations.idiomatic: Approaching Ye, Hui wept on horseback and threw himself to earth, blood covering his face.

sentences.zh: 至長安，尋與後主同死。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, he soon died together with Houzhu.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he soon died together with Houzhu.

sentences.zh: 妃盧氏，賜斛斯徵，蓬首垢面，長齋不言笑。

translations.literal: His consort Lady Lu was given to Husi Zheng; disheveled and filthy, she kept long fasts and neither spoke nor smiled.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Lu was given to Husi Zheng; unkempt and mute, she kept long fasts and neither spoke nor smiled.

sentences.zh: 徵放之，乃為尼。

translations.literal: When Zheng released her, she became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng released her, she took the tonsure.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇三年，表請文帝葬湝及五子於長安北原。

translations.literal: In the third year of Sui's Kaihuang era she petitioned Emperor Wen to bury Hui and his five sons on the north plain of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Kaihuang era of Sui she petitioned Emperor Wen to bury Hui and his five sons on Chang'an's north plain.

sentences.zh: 高陽康穆王湜，神武第十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang (Shi) was the eleventh son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 十年，稍遷尚書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was gradually promoted to Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he rose to chief minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以滑稽便辟，有寵于文宣，常在左右，行杖以撻諸王。

translations.literal: Because he was glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Wenxuan's favor, always attended him, and walked about beating the other princes with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Gao Yang's favor, kept always at his side, and carried a staff with which he beat the other princes.

sentences.zh: 太后深銜之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 其妃父護軍長史張晏之嘗要道拜湜，湜不禮焉。

translations.literal: His consort's father, Chief Commandant's Senior Aide Zhang Yanzi, once stopped the road to pay respects to Shi; Shi did not return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His consort's father, chief commandant's senior aide Zhang Yanzi, once intercepted the road to pay respects; Shi did not return them.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，對曰：「無官職漢，何須禮。

translations.literal: When the Emperor asked why, Shi answered, "A Han man with no office — why should I show courtesy?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Shi said, "A commoner without office — why should I bow?"

sentences.zh: 」帝於是擢拜晏之為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon promoted Yanzi to Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly made Yanzi governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 文宣崩，兼司徒，導引梓宮，吹笛，云「至尊頗知臣不」，又擊胡鼓為樂。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan died Shi served concurrently as Minister of Works, led the imperial coffin, played the flute, and said, "The sovereign surely knew his servant," also beating the Hu drum for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang died Shi served as minister of works, led the coffin procession, played the flute saying "The sovereign knew me well," and beat the Hu drum for sport.

sentences.zh: 太后杖湜百餘，未幾薨。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had Shi beaten more than a hundred strokes; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had him beaten more than a hundred strokes; he died shortly after.

sentences.zh: 太后哭之哀，曰：「我恐其不成就，與杖，何期帶創死也！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept bitterly and said, "I feared he would never amount to anything and beat him — who dreamed he would die of his wounds!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept bitterly: "I feared he would never amount to anything and struck him — who dreamed the blows would kill him!"

sentences.zh: 」乾明初，贈假黃鉞、太師、司徒、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Qianming era he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, minister of works, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子士義襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shiyi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyi inherited.

sentences.zh: 博陵文簡王濟，神武第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenjian of Boling (Ji) was the twelfth son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 濟嘗從文宣巡幸，在路忽憶太后，遂逃歸。

translations.literal: Ji once accompanied Wenxuan on tour; on the road he suddenly remembered the Empress Dowager and fled back home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji once accompanied Gao Yang on tour; on the road he suddenly missed the empress dowager and fled home.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，臨以白刃，因此驚恍。

translations.literal: The Emperor in rage threatened him with naked blades, and from this Ji was seized with terror and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor threatened him with naked steel; from that shock Ji was never right again.

sentences.zh: 歷位太尉。

translations.literal: He held office through the rank of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He served through the rank of grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 河清初，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Heqing he was sent out as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Heqing era he was made governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 天統五年，在州語人云：「計次第亦應到我。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong, at his post he told people, "By the count of succession my turn ought to come."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tiantong era he told people at his post, "By order of succession it should be my turn next."

sentences.zh: 」後主聞之，陰使人殺之。

translations.literal: Houzhu heard of it and secretly had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu heard and secretly had him killed.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子智襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 馮翊王潤，字子澤，神武第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Fengyi, Run, style name Zize, was the fourteenth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fengyi (Run), whose style name was Zize, was the fourteenth son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 幼時，神武稱曰：「此吾家千里駒也。

translations.literal: In youth Shenwu called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."
translations.idiomatic: In boyhood Gao Huan called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."

sentences.zh: 」天保初封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed at the opening of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 歷位東北道大行臺、右僕射、都督、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He held office successively as Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Northeast Road, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Area Commander, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as northeast-route grand mobile headquarters, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, area commander, and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 潤美姿儀，年十四五，母鄭妃與之同寢，有穢雜之聲。

translations.literal: Run had handsome looks; at fourteen or fifteen his mother Consort Zheng slept with him in the same bed, and obscene sounds were heard.
translations.idiomatic: Run was handsome; at fourteen or fifteen he shared a bed with his mother Consort Zheng, and lewd sounds were heard.

sentences.zh: 及長，廉慎方雅，習於吏職，至摘發隱偽，姦吏無所匿其情。

translations.literal: When grown he was upright, cautious, and refined, skilled in official business; even in exposing hidden fraud no corrupt clerk could conceal the facts from him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was upright, cautious, and skilled in office; in exposing hidden fraud no clerk could hide from him.

sentences.zh: 開府王迴洛與六州大都督獨孤枝侵竊官田，受納賄賂，潤按舉其事。

translations.literal: Opener of the Way Wang Huiluo and Six-Province Commander-in-Chief Dugu Zhi encroached on public land and accepted bribes; Run investigated and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Opener of the way Wang Huiluo and six-province commander-in-chief Dugu Zhi had encroached on public land and taken bribes; Run investigated and impeached them.

sentences.zh: 二人表言，王出送臺使，登魏文舊壇，南望歎息，不測其意。

translations.literal: The two submitted a memorial saying that when the prince saw off a capital envoy he climbed the old platform of Emperor Wen of Wei, looked south, and sighed — none could fathom his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The two memorialized that when Run saw off a capital envoy he climbed Cao Pi's old platform, gazed south, and sighed — no one could read his mind.

sentences.zh: 武成使元文遙就州宣勑曰：「馮翊王少小謹慎，在州不為非法，朕信之熟矣。

translations.literal: Wucheng sent Yuan Wenyao to the province with an edict, saying, "Prince of Fengyi Run has been careful from youth; at his post he has committed no wrong — I know him well.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan sent Yuan Wenyao with an edict: "Prince Run has been careful from youth and committed no crime in office — I know him thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 登高遠望，人之常情，鼠輩欲橫相間構，曲生眉目。

translations.literal: To climb high and gaze far is human nature; vermin trying to invent slander and twist facts out of nothing."
translations.idiomatic: To climb high and look far is only human; these vermin would invent treason out of thin air."

sentences.zh: 」於是回洛決鞭二百，獨孤枝決杖一百。

translations.literal: Huiluo was sentenced to two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi to one hundred strokes with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Huiluo received two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi one hundred strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，領太子少師，歷司徒、太尉、大司馬、司州牧、太保、河南道行台、領錄尚書，別封文成郡公、太師、太宰，復為定州刺史。

translations.literal: He soon became Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Tutor, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Road, and Concurrent Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Preceptor of the Realm — and again made Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor of the crown prince, then minister of works, grand commandant, grand marshal, governor of Si Province, grand tutor, Henan-route grand mobile headquarters, and recorder of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Wencheng, grand preceptor and grand preceptor of the realm — and again made governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞、左丞相。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe and Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe and left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 子茂德嗣。

translations.literal: His son Maode succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maode succeeded.

sentences.zh: 漢陽敬懷王洽，字敬延，神武第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, style name Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang (Qia), whose style name was Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 天保元年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 五年，薨，年十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，贈太保、司空。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianming he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era he was posthumously made grand tutor and minister of works.

sentences.zh: 無子，以任城王第二子建德為後。

translations.literal: Having no sons, the second son of the Prince of Rencheng, Jiande, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, Jiande, second son of the Prince of Rencheng, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the standard for collation.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout, this text has been collated against the first Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
